correction.text: 'a core territory in the region of Kanem (northeast of Lake Chad)'

keyframe_review.note: Review af-03-a: the Cliopatria shape is not used. Its 20,167 km2 (15.1-16.7 E, 11.3-12.6 N) lie south-east of Lake Chad and share no cell with the gazetteer's region Kanem (13.5-17.9 E, 13.1-16.8 N); they do not contain the capital point Njimi (the Mao proxy, 15.31 E, 14.12 N) either. The page: 'with a core territory in the region of Kanem (northeast of Lake Chad)'; 'The empire's first capital was probably Njimi ... east of Lake Chad'. So 1072-1249 is drawn as the region Kanem (about 134,000 km2; the page gives no area, so the infobox check is not possible, and the region is a generous container for the core). (My first note called the Cliopatria shape 'a seventh' of Kanem; that was wrong, the two are disjoint.) The page puts the foundation c. 700 under the Duguwa and the change to the Sayfawa in 'the second half of the 11th century' under mai Hummay; 1072 is Cliopatria's first year (bridge). The same Cliopatria outline runs on to 1374; the next entries replace it for 1250-1374.

The page gives no year and no taker; 1350 reads 'the middle of the 14th century'. The Fezzan page (second page) says only 'During the 13th and 14th centuries, the Fezzan became a part of the Kanem Empire, which extended as far as Zella, Libya', with no end year and no taker, and puts the wars against Kanem-Bornu that founded the Awlad Muhammad dynasty in the early sixteenth century.

c. 1380: Njimi is abandoned and the empire moves to Bornu. 'Njimi ... abandoned after c. 1380'; 'After the fall of Njimi, the empire lacked a permanent capital for about a century.'
c. 1472: Mai Ali founds Ngazargamu. 'In c. 1472, Ali founded the empire's first substantial capital city, Ngazargamu.'

Review af-03-a (author's addition): the region is narrowed from the whole of Kanem to the part inside Cliopatria's 1487 shape, which is all that the drawing holds from 1500 to 1890 (135-137 of the region's 531 cells); the pages have the Bilala still ruling part of Kanem under Alooma ('a peace agreement was reached with Abdullah, the Bilala mai of Kanem', with 'clear demarcations') and driven out only c. 1630 by Wadai. The year stays the page's 'early 1500s', the region is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: The Kanem frontier is settled by treaty: 'a peace agreement was reached with Abdullah, the Bilala mai of Kanem', with 'clear demarcations to define the borders'. The page gives no year; 1603 is the end of Alooma's reign.

The page does not list the lost districts and does not say how much territory was lost; the region is the difference between Cliopatria's 1808 and 1809 shapes (the researcher's reading, hence confidence 2). The Fulani War page names no district lost in 1809; its Hadejia, Katagum, Jamaare and Misau remark is about a late-18th-century district of western Bornu. (Review af-03-a: the Deya district was dropped from the region text; the al-Kanemi page has al-Kanemi occupying 'the Deya- Damaturu area' later in the 1820s, not the Fulani taking it.)

Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the page names three towns and not the province of Extrême-Nord, which is used as the drawable container. Review af-03-a: the counterpart is the Kotoko city states, which the page names; it does not say that Bagirmi held them.

region.text: Ngazargamu and the heart of Bornu

ledger.note: Later in the 1820s: the Fulani are driven out of Bornu. 'Later in the 1820s, al-Kanemi drove the Fulani out of Bornu.' The page gives no year; 1827 is a bridge. Second pages (opened 2026-10-19): the Kanem-Bornu page has 'The Fulani were driven away from the empire and mai Dunama was restored to power' and 'Al-Kanemi supported Dunama's restoration in 1814' without a year for the expulsion; the Fulani War page does not describe the expulsion. The al-Kanemi page's 'Later in the 1820s' and the Kanem-Bornu page's order of events do not match; 1827 stays a bridge.

1846: the al-Kanemi shehus replace the Sayfawa mais. Infobox: 'Ali V Minargema, last mai (1846)'; 'Umar Kura, de jure first (1837/1846-1881)'; al-Kanemi had been 'de facto first' since 1814. (The Fulani War page calls this the 'toppling of the Sayfawa dynasty in 1846' and counts it among the jihadists' expansions, which does not match the Kanem-Bornu page.)

May 1893: Rabih az-Zubayr invades Bornu. 'The two armies clashed at the battle of Amja, in May 1893'; 'In 1892-1894, Rabih conquered the Kanem-Bornu Empire'; he sacked Kukawa and 'The beginning of Rabih's rule over Bornu would later be dated to 2 October'.

February/March 1894: Rabih beats Kyari on the Yobe. 'In February/March 1894, Rabih intercepted Kyari's army near Gashegar, on the southern bank of the Yobe River'; Kyari was captured and later killed.
1894: Bornu passes to Rabih. 'In 1893, Kanem-Bornu was conquered by the Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr' (Kanem-Bornu page); he 'transformed it into a military dictatorship'.

1894: the Kanem-Bornu Empire ends as an independent state. Rabih was beaten and killed at Kousseri on 22 April 1900; the shehus were reinstated in 1900 'under colonial suzerainty'; the territory 'fell completely under colonial control in 1902'.

wars.name: Fulani jihad against Bornu

zones.text: Ngazargamu and the heart of Bornu

the south-western borderlands between Cliopatria's 1808 and 1809 shapes (the researcher's reading; the page says only that 'the Bornu Fulani began advancing further into Bornu territory'; the Fulani War page's Galadima Dunama district 'encompassed portions of what later became the emirates of Hadejia, Katagum, Jamaare, and Misau')

wars.outcome: The Fulani destroyed Ngazargamu in 1808 and held the south-western districts; Muhammad al-Kanemi saved the mai and 'later in the 1820s' drove the Fulani out of Bornu proper.
wars.note: The jihad itself dates from 21 February 1804 (Fulani War page); its sack of Ngazargamu is 1808.

wars.name: Bornu-Bagirmi war

zones.text: Kousseri, Ngulfai and Logone, the Kotoko cities (the province as container)

wars.outcome: Al-Kanemi defeated Bagirmi in 1824 and occupied Kousseri, Ngulfai and Logone.
wars.note: Review af-03-a: the page names three Kotoko towns, not the province; it does not say who held them before 1824.

wars.name: Rabih's conquest of Bornu
wars.outcome: Rabih took Kukawa in 1893 (Amja, May 1893; Lekarawa about August) and beat Kyari at Dimurwa on the Yobe in February/March 1894; Bornu became his military dictatorship.
wars.note: In 1892 he had beaten a joint Bagirmi-Wadai army.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier of Kanem or Bornu; the Sahel and Lake Chad margins are approximate. The Kanem border with the Bilala was 'demarcated' under Alooma but no line is given.

notes: ONE STATE, TWO CLIOPATRIA ROWS: 'Empire of Kanem' (1072-1384) and 'Bornu Empire' (1385-1894) share Wikidata Q1139762 and one Wikipedia article (Kanem-Bornu Empire), which treats them as a single empire and one Sayfawa dynasty that moved from Kanem to Bornu c. 1380. They are merged here under the earlier slug empire-of-kanem; the slug bornu-empire therefore has no dossier of its own and counterpart references to 'bornu-empire' in other groups' dossiers (wadai-empire, sokoto-caliphate) should use empire-of-kanem. The Cliopatria shape ids of the Bornu rows (bornu-empire_1385 ... bornu-empire_1890) are reviewed here unchanged. Corrections: (1) a zenith keyframe 1250-1349 (Kanem, Bornu, Fezzan) from the Dunama and Kanem-Bornu pages, with the Kano and Ouaddai claims left as influence; (2) Kanem outline ends 1380 and the Bornu core runs from 1381 (the page's 'around 1380'); (3) the region Kanem is taken out of the Bornu shapes of 1482-1499 and returns in 1500 (page: 'early 1500s'; Cliopatria has it from 1482); (4) Alooma-era 'influence' over Hausaland, Aïr, Bilma, Tibesti is not drawn (undated, no borders); (5) 1809 loss to the Fulani is read from Cliopatria's two shapes. Not settled: no page opened gives an area for any year (no infobox check possible); the 1385, 1482, 1487, 1579, 1636 and 1811 shape changes are barely explained; the 1630 Wadai drive of the Bilala from Kanem is not tied to a Bornu border change; the dates of Umar I Idrismi, Ali I Gaji, Idris III Katagarmabe and Alooma's expeditions are 'approximately' or absent; no ruler strip because no list with years was opened (infobox gives Susam c. 700, Muhammad al-Kanemi 1814-1837, Umar Kura 1837/1846-1881, Ali V Minargema 1846, Abubakar Garbai 1900-1902). The Fulani War page's remark that the Sayfawa were toppled by the jihadists in 1846 conflicts with the Kanem-Bornu page (a shehu coup). Counterparts needing dossiers: state-of-rabih-az-zubayr (c. 1892-1900), bagirmi-sultanate, Bilala (Bulala) kingdom of Kanem (c. 1380-1630+). Gazetteer names needed: Njimi, Kukawa, Kafela (Kafela's 1809-1813 and 1813-1846 seat of the mais is a dot not given), Amsaka. The Wadai Empire and Sokoto Caliphate pages were not opened by this batch. REVIEW FIXES (af-03-a, 2026-10-19): (a) Cliopatria's Empire of Kanem outline (1072-1384, 20,167 km2, 15.1-16.7 E, 11.3-12.6 N) is disjoint from the page's Kanem (no shared cell with the gazetteer region Kanem; it does not contain Njimi), so the region Kanem is drawn for 1072-1249 and, with the Bornu core, for 1350-1380; (b) the zenith keyframe now draws Bornu as the Bornu core of Cliopatria's 1385 shape (a new entry 1350-1374 and the 1375 entry carry Kanem and that core without the Fezzan), so nothing disappears in 1350 and nothing shrinks in 1381 apart from Kanem; Dunama's reach 'as far south as Mafoni in modern day Borno State' is a gap (the gazetteer has no Mafoni and a whole Borno State would reopen an unexplained drop at 1385); (c) the 1482 and 1487 corrections subtract the gazetteer region Kanem, and the 1500 gain is narrowed to the quarter of Kanem that Cliopatria's 1487-1890 shapes hold (author's addition; the Bilala kept the rest); (d) ledger 1809 and 1824 texts and the 1824 counterpart follow the pages' words. Still undated on the pages opened: the Bornu incorporation under Dunama, the end of the Fezzan grip, Alooma's Kanem expeditions and the Bilala treaty, the expulsion of the Fulani.
